paper_title: Context Consistency between Training and Testing in Simultaneous Machine   Translation
caption: : Caption not extracted
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between BLEU score and average lagging (AL) for four different models, with the x-axis representing average lagging (AL) on a linear scale ranging from 2.5 to 12.5, and the y-axis representing BLEU score on a linear scale from 25 to 33. The plot includes four distinct lines: Consistency-CE, represented by a light purple line with circular markers; Inconsistency-CE, shown as a dark purple line with square markers; Inconsistency-CE-MP, depicted as a dark blue line with square markers and a dashed line style; and Consistency-Bi, shown as a red line with star markers and a solid line style. All four lines exhibit an increasing trend as average lagging increases. At an average lagging of 2.5, the BLEU scores are approximately 25.8 for Consistency-CE, 26.0 for Inconsistency-CE, 26.2 for Inconsistency-CE-MP, and 28.9 for Consistency-Bi. At an average lagging of 12.5, the BLEU scores reach approximately 31.5 for Consistency-CE, 31.6 for Inconsistency-CE, 32.1 for Inconsistency-CE-MP, and 32.2 for Consistency-Bi. The Consistency-Bi model consistently achieves the highest BLEU score across the entire range of average lagging values, while the Consistency-CE model consistently achieves the lowest BLEU score.
